subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & Performance SLOs — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's perf qualification call

Sam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of ask:
- You want a reproducible benchmark that validates production SLOs for the model serving path (hosted/dedicated) focusing on latency (p95), sustained throughput, concurrency behavior, and streaming tail correctness.
- Target SLOs voiced on the call: p95 latency <= 250ms for single-turn generation, ability to sustain ~200 qps with up to 50 concurrent sessions for your highest-throughput endpoints, and streaming chunk order/latency within 100ms of token generation for client streaming.

What we'll provide:
- Benchmark methodology doc (measurement definitions, warmup, steady-state window, error handling).
- A reproducible eval harness (Docker + scripts) and the prompt set you used during the call for parity.
- Standardized reporting (p50/p90/p95/p99, token-level metrics, concurrency breakdowns) and the raw logs so your infra team can verify results.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) We'll share the benchmark harness + prompt set by end of day tomorrow (attached).
2) You provide a short sample of representative requests (anonymized) and any streaming client behavior we should emulate (chunk sizes, inter-chunk timing).
3) Schedule a 2-hour bench run window next week — we suggest Tues 24 Aug, 09:00–11:00 PT (Redwood will run on a Dedicated pool and share live metrics).

Questions for you:
- Confirm the p95 and target qps above or send any adjustments.
- Any security/compliance constraints for the harness (static IP allowlist, corp proxy, or data handling requirements)?

Attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt set), redwood_benchmark_harness_v2.tar.gz (harness).

Thanks — looking forward to validating this quickly.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeFin Platform <platform@edgefin.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's perf qualification call

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

Confirmed SLOs:
- p95 end-to-end (request -> final token) <= 250ms for single-turn generation (this includes network and any middleware).
- Sustained throughput goal: 200 qps across the service with 50 concurrency for burst scenario (we expect traffic to be spiky).
- Streaming: client requires token chunking such that each chunk arrives within 100ms from the token generation event; we can provide a sample client to emulate this.

Security/compliance:
- We need the benchmark harness to run within our VPC or from Redwood's dedicated environment with traffic exiting to our monitor IPs (we'll provide allowlist).
- No PII in samples — we'll provide an anonymized set.

Two asks:
1) Can you include measurement definitions for warmup vs steady-state and how you compute p95 for streaming endpoints? We want to be sure we compare apples to apples.
2) Is Redwood able to provide raw token-level timestamps (anonymized) so we can run our own post-hoc analysis?

We'll aim to get the anonymized samples and allowlist by EOD Monday. Tuesday window works for us — please confirm timezone/offset and the pool you'll use.

— Sam
Head of Platform
EdgeFin
sam.patel@edgefin.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's perf qualification call

Sam — thanks, noted. A few clarifications and what we'll deliver in the harness package:

Measurement definitions (included in the harness README):
- Warmup: first 120s of synthetic traffic are discarded. No metrics reported for warmup.
- Steady-state window: 10-minute sliding window after warmup used for percentile calculations.
- pXX calculation: per-request end-to-end latency measured at the Redwood edge; for streaming endpoints we'll compute per-token generation timestamps and derive per-request p95 by using the time of the final token emitted. We will also report token-level p50/p90/p95 for the first-token and subsequent tokens to surface cold-token tails.
- Errors: any 5xx or protocol disconnect is counted as an error; error rate reported separately.

Data access: we can provide anonymized token-level timestamps (scrubbed of PII) as gzipped CSV in the report. If you'd prefer to run the harness inside your VPC, we can hand off the Docker artifact and a short runbook.

Pool & scheduling:
- We'll run the official validation on a Redwood Dedicated pool (GPU type: A100x2 equivalent) during the Tue 24 Aug 09:00–11:00 PT window unless you ask otherwise. Live dashboard link (read-only) will be shared 30 minutes before start.

Attachments in this email: SLA template (sla_requirements.xlsx). Hub links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink

If that all looks good, we'll proceed to share the harness and a short checklist for your infra team.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
